parts:
Hi Marco,

I'm splitting this thread into two, because your two questions are unrelated.

On Thu, Nov 19, 2009 at 10:01 AM, marco <mazu...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Dear Herink,
>
>  I have 2 technical questions (I saw something similar regarding older
> versions).
>
> I generated a cesN set, extracted some arrays that I want to average:
>
> ###
> cesA <- extract(cesN, c(1:2))
>
> cesEX <- extract(cesN, c(7:9))
> sc364 <- calculateBaseline(cesEX, chromosomes=1:23,
> ploidy=2,defaultPloidy=2);
>
> cesEX <- extract(cesN, c(14:18))
> sc368 <- calculateBaseline(cesEX, chromosomes=1:23,
> ploidy=2,defaultPloidy=2);
> ###
>
> First question is what is the difference between calculateBaseline()
> and getAverageFile(),
>
> 1. calculateBaseline() usese median to pool the arrays?

Yes.
The calculateBaseline() method calculates reference signals as
described in Section 3.2.7 'Reference signals' in [1]. Simply
speaking, it uses the median of the pool of all samples to calculate
the average/baseline/diploid (CN=2) reference signal at each locus.
To do this, it uses getAverageFile(). The difference is that for ChrX
and ChrY, where males and females have difference expected mean
levels, that does not work. Traditionally it has been suggested to
only use female samples to estimate CN=2 for ChrX, but the method we
proposed in [1] utilizes the males to by recognizing that their
signals are lower by can still contribute to the estimate of the CN=2
level *per locus*. It works as long as you have at least one female.
The gain is that the noise level is decreased. See [1] for
details/rationales.

In order for this to work, your males and females arrays have to have
tags 'XY' and 'XX'. Alternatively, you can use so called attributes,
which we haven't pushed much because they are still under development.
However, you can read more about this in the Vignette 'Sex-chromosome
bias-corrected reference signals from pooled average':

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/sex-chromosome-bias-corrected-reference-signals-from-pooled-average

> 2. getAverageFile uses the "mean" ? Does it take care of sex
> chromosome ploidy?

No, getAverageFile() uses median by default. It does not take care of
the sex chromosomes; it is completely unaware about the biology and
only does what it says - it calculates the average across files
(=arrays).

>
[snip]

REFERENCES:

[1] H. Bengtsson, R. Irizarry, B. Carvalho & T.P. Speed, Estimation
and assessment of raw copy numbers at the single locus level,
Bioinformatics 2008﻿﻿, 24, pp759-767.

/Henrik

> Best Regards
>
> Marco
